answer: Divergent-history attestation: each identity publishes a signed hash chain of daily cedar-keyed commitments, and peers accept an action only if its chain diverges correctly from a shared reference after a random delta delay. A sybil cluster must run every clone through distinct honest histories to pass comparison, and one mismatch flags all. An attacker pays full per-identity compute and storage to fabricate divergent chains plus a velvet-soft registration bond forfeited on any inconsistency, so N clones cost N times a real agent's ongoing upkeep.
